context: A semantic zoom scatterplot showing 2000 points across 4 clusters (Alpha/Beta/Gamma/Delta), with three progressive LOD modes triggered by scroll zoom: density contours at low zoom (k<3.5), hexbins at medium zoom (k=3.5–10), and individual SVG points with tooltips at high zoom (k>10). Hysteresis prevents LOD flickering.
first_impression: Clean and immediately readable — four distinct cluster blobs are clearly separated in the contour view with no visual clutter.
what_works: The LOD progression is conceptually well-matched to zoom level: contours give gestalt shape, hexbins reveal cluster dominance and density, points enable individual inspection. The monochromatic blue contour view keeps cognitive load minimal at the overview level.
what_doesnt: Contour mode loses all categorical (cluster) identity — all four clusters render in the same blue gradient, so the viewer cannot tell Alpha from Delta without zooming in; this breaks the legend-to-mark matching that the 4-color TOL palette is designed to provide. Static screenshot cannot assess whether the LOD mode transitions (contours → hex → points) feel abrupt or smooth in motion, which is the central perceptual risk of this design.
